spiritual_reading:
¶1–2 — The Light Mind entering the flesh; the bound “old man” and recurrent rebellions
Correspondential objects: Light/Mind; “coming” and “assuming” saints; body of flesh; “old man”; binding/chaining; five counsels; five limbs.
Spiritual realities: “Light” is truth/wisdom in the spiritual degree; “Mind” is the formed organ of reception of that light (understanding ordered by heaven). “Coming/assuming” is influx clothing itself in ultimates. The “body of flesh” is the natural mind as an ultimate receptacle; the “old man” is the hereditary proprium (the old will and its falsities) lodged in that natural. “Binding” is restraint by order—truth placing limits on disorder. The “five counsels/limbs” are the fixed faculties in ultimates through which life acts (the natural’s operative powers), now to be governed.
Movement: A new ruling principle (Light Mind) descends into the natural degree and begins re-ordering by fastening its governance into the life’s outer functions; yet because the old proprium remains present, disturbances (“rebellions”) still arise—showing that restraint is not yet full regeneration.

¶3–6, 9–10 — The scandal of the Infinite in the finite; invisibility of the indwelling; persecution; promise of opened sight and fountain
Correspondential objects: “great God… unchanging… immeasurable”; “smallness of the body”; “holy… pure” versus “defilement”; “likeness not displayed”; oppression/persecution in the world; “repeat… understand”; “vision to they who see”; “living fountain” for thirsty.
Spiritual realities: The “immeasurable” is the Divine/Heavenly in its own degree; “small body” is the narrow natural form. The question about defilement is the question of whether pure influx can remain pure in impure ultimates. “Likeness not displayed” is the law that internals are not seen except through correspondences perceived by an opened understanding. “Persecution in the world” is resistance from the external man and the surrounding falsities when truth begins to rule. “Vision” is enlightenment; “fountain” is living truth flowing into the natural for use.
Movement: The text turns from natural reasoning (“how can the great be in the small?”) to the doctrine of perception: true sight is given by an opened organ, and living truth must overflow to sustain the thirsty natural. The Lord’s influx does not become visible as an object; it becomes visible as understanding.

¶11–13 — The enemy’s construction “after the likeness of a man”: the cosmos in the form of the perverted Grand Man
Correspondential objects: “enemy of the lights”; “constructed… after the likeness of a man”; head/neck/stomach/ribs/navel/loins/shins/feet; garments; firmaments; sphere of stars/zodiac; four worlds; three earths; “Porter”; heart/liver/lung/spleen/kidneys; animals (four-footed, birds, fish, reptiles); outer skin as wall around “piercing” and “great fire”; vessels of fire; darkness; intestines; veins as springs and wells.
Spiritual realities: “Man” here is not merely an individual but the doctrine of the Grand Human (Maximus Homo): heaven and the church in one form. In opposite sense, the “enemy” imitates that form, producing a counterfeit order: a system that looks human (coherent) but is ruled by self and falsity.
Body-part correspondences: head = ruling love/primary principle; neck = communication of that ruling into lower things; ribs/firmaments = general truths that hold interiors in order; navel/stars = knowledges and their constellations (scientifics and doctrinals) that connect higher to lower; loins/three earths = generative powers in ultimates (productive natural planes); feet/shins = lowest natural supports. Heart = the will of the community (mankind) as the central affection; liver/lung/spleen/kidneys as various natural affections and purifications—here mapped to animal kingdoms (affections in ultimates). Springs and wells = the derivations of truth in the natural mind. “Great fire” is love; in this context it is guarded/contained as a dangerous perimeter, hinting at self-love’s consuming fire. Darkness is falsity/ignorance in ultimates.
Movement: The chapter reveals that disorder is not random: hellish falsity constructs a total system in the form of a human, because all reality must appear in that form; the difference is the ruling love. This prepares the later teaching: the same body can be made a “new man” when reordered by true influx.

¶14–18 — The placement of watch-keepers: discrete degrees stabilized; counsel over wind, fire, water; the making of “camps”
Correspondential objects: Keeper of Splendour; “mind above”; powers of heaven; King of Honour in “seventh firmament”; Adamant of Light as “insight”; King of Glory as “counsel… patience”; three images/wheels of wind, fire, water; Porter as consideration/wisdom “below”; foundation; Ambassador; five intellectuals of life; summons/obedience; six sons of Living Spirit and of First Man; great Mind as Pillar of Glory/Perfect Man; Jesus the Youth as image of living word/utterance/obedience; camps above and below; circuits and watch-districts; security against uprising/treachery.
Spiritual realities: This is the architecture of ordered influx through discrete degrees.
- “Above” denotes interior degrees; “below” denotes ultimates.
- “Firmaments” are general spiritual truths that separate and mediate degrees.
- Watch-keepers are governing principles (providential restraints and ordered functions) stationed at each level.
- Wind/breath = influx and the movement of life; water = truths in the natural; fire = love/will. To place “patience/counsel” over wind, fire, water is to subject influx, love, and truth to steady governance so ascent (elevation) can occur.
- “Porter” corresponds to the ultimate gate-function: the natural mind’s threshold and its orderly admissions.
- “Ambassador” is mediating Divine truth proceeding—doctrine/instruction that arranges recipients.
- “Pillar of Glory/Perfect Man” is the formed heavenly human in ultimates: truth and good conjoined in a stable support.
- “Word/utterance/obedience” are the external expressions of internal truth: doctrine articulated and lived.
Movement: The text depicts Providence establishing a hierarchical guard: interior principles fixed in their stations so that the system can be held in form. This is the blueprint of regeneration: loves and truths must be stationed, mediated, and secured, otherwise every degree becomes a site of revolt.

¶19–23 — Uprisings in the watch-districts: how falsity breaks out into dry and moist, sea and earth; disclosure of “crafts”; lust filling the world
Correspondential objects: gloom of death; Sin aborting; tangling with soul; mixed light; third firmament; dry and moist; trees on dry land; sea uprising; wrath; watchers descending; crafts and mysteries unveiled; abortions falling; Adam and Eve formed; objects of lust; three wheels/earths; paths closed; ascent impeded; wind/water/fire impeded; abysses below; loosened fastenings; foundation.
Spiritual realities: “Uprising/treachery” is inversion of order—lower ruling over higher. “Gloom of death” is the extinguishing of spiritual life by falsity. “Sin tangling with the soul” is falsity conjoining to affection in the natural. “Dry” is truth without good (barren understanding); “moist” is truth with some life (receptive natural). “Trees” are perceptions/knowledges grown from seeds of truth; in opposite sense they are reasonings and memory-knowledges that spring up from mixed light. “Sea” is the general natural mind and its mass of knowledges; uprising in the sea is tumult in the natural-knowledges and sensuous thought.
“Watchers descending” corresponds to knowledges and intellectual powers turned outward into mere worldly ends, corrupting by “crafts” (skills severed from charity) and divulging “mysteries of heaven” as profaned doctrinals. “Abortions” are falsified births—concepts and desires produced without legitimate conjunction of good and truth. “Adam and Eve” here are the initial forms of the human mind (will and understanding) as seized by falsity for domination. “Three wheels/earths” are the cyclical operations of life in ultimates; when “paths close,” ascent of wind/water/fire means influx, truth, and love are impeded from rising back toward the interior.
“Loosened fastenings” and “abysses” describe the collapse of ultimate restraints: the natural foundations no longer hold spiritual order.
Movement: Even with watch-keepers, when the lower is permitted to act for a time, falsity spreads into every plane: into barren understanding (dry), into natural receptivity (moist), into the tumult of knowledges (sea), into the generative powers (lust). The result is blocked ascent—influx can enter, but cannot be returned in obedience; hence disorder multiplies.

¶24–29 — Remedies by higher influx: Pillar bearing burdens; binding with chains; descent of Jesus; opening springs and setting ascent; strengthening fastenings
Correspondential objects: earthquake; Pillar of Glory coming forth; burdens; four angels; eternal chain; prison of blackened ones; obliterating children; Jesus sent; prayer of five sons; assuming them; fastening beneath mind of Adam; Jesus casting himself down; assuming Eve; straightening tracks; opening springs of wind/water/fire; ordering ascent; reaching loosened foundation; strengthening fastenings; return to rest; humiliations until enmity humbled.
Spiritual realities: “Earthquake” is upheaval in the natural mind when its foundations are shaken—either by hellish assault or by the reordering action of truth. “Pillar of Glory” is the stabilizing ultimate of heaven: the Divine Human in the natural degree bearing the whole weight of reformation. “Four angels” are universal guards at the quarters—general truths that restrain falsity in all directions of the mind. “Chains” are binding by fixed truths; “prison” is confinement of falsities to their own sphere so they cannot spread.
“Jesus” here functions as Divine truth accommodated to ultimates—the saving descent into the natural’s lowest states. “Assuming Eve” is taking up the external affection (natural delight) and reforming it; “straightening tracks” is rectifying the pathways of influx; “opening springs” is restoring the derivations of truth (water), the movement of life (wind), and the warmth of love (fire) so they can ascend—i.e., so the natural can respond and be elevated.
“Strengthening fastenings” is re-establishing ultimate moral/cognitive restraints so higher order can rest upon them.
Movement: Providence answers revolt not by abandoning the lowest, but by descending into it: binding what must be bound, restoring circulation (springs and tracks), and rebuilding foundations. The system is humbled—brought back under rule—through repeated interventions until the enemy’s power is subordinated.

¶30–32 — The macrocosm explains the microcosm: the same law in the body; permitted disturbances under righteous judgment
Correspondential objects: “this body”; mighty power in small stature; Sin dwelling within; old man lodged; watch-district of Mind; agitations; powers of light; beginning and end unveiled; permitting enmity for a moment; then seizing.
Spiritual realities: The “zone” with its watch-districts is the human organism of mind and body. The “mighty power” in the small body is interior influx (spiritual/celestial) operating in a narrow natural receptacle. “Permitting for a moment” is Divine permission according to order: evils are allowed to come forth so they can be seen, judged, and then restrained; thus reformation is not magic but lawful.
Movement: The chapter explicitly applies the cosmological pattern to personal regeneration: periodic disturbances in the natural do not disprove the presence of Light; they are the necessary exposures within providential governance.

¶33–34 (implicit) — Great in the small: enclosure like trees holding a taproot
Correspondential objects: gods “enclosed and hard pressed”; trees; taproot; place set.
Spiritual realities: “Tree” is perception/knowledge formed into living structure; “taproot” is the inmost connection to the source (celestial love feeding the whole). To be “enclosed” is to be terminated in an ultimate form; spiritual forces must be fixed in a plane to act. The Divine can be present in the finite because it acts by correspondences: interior life holds to its taproot while operating in the assigned plane.
Movement: The paradox is resolved: greatness is not diminished by ultimate clothing; rather, it becomes operative. Influx is made determinate by being set in its “place.”

¶35–37 — Sin’s counterfeit binding: five members; soul-forgetfulness; idolatry and unclean beasts
Correspondential objects: five members; bone/sinew/vein/flesh/skin; mind/thought/insight/counsel/consideration; five powers of sin set upon five of the soul; angels/authorities; leading to lust, idols; wood/gold/silver; unclean beasts; error and forgetfulness; forgetting essence/race/kindred; not knowing the door of prayer; hostility to father; own light.
Spiritual realities: The natural body-parts correspond to successive ultimates of reception.
- Bone = the hardest supports: fixed natural truths or mere rigid principles (in opposite sense, dead ultimates).
- Sinew = connective power: the binding of ideas into action.
- Vein = conduits of life in the natural: pathways of thought and affection in the external.
- Flesh = the living substance of the natural will.
- Skin = the outermost boundary: sensuous and external memory-knowledges that define the person’s interface with the world.
Sin’s “five powers” are a parody of the soul’s faculties: falsity enthroned upon understanding, evil upon will, so that the whole external man is governed.
“Idols of wood/gold/silver” are worship of mere external goods and truths divorced from the Divine: wood = natural good, gold = celestial good, silver = spiritual truth; in idolatry these are severed from their source and adored as self-originating. “Unclean beasts” are defiled affections.
“Forgetfulness” is loss of internal remembrance—no perception of origin (“father”), no knowledge of the “door” (the genuine admission to heaven: prayer and humble turning), thus hostility to one’s own light.
Movement: The text shows how bondage works: evil does not only entice; it installs itself into the very ultimates of thinking and acting, producing a closed system in which the soul cannot even recognize its own lineage or how to turn upward.

¶38–40 — The Light Mind’s work: reversal by correspondential rebinding; construction of the new man; placing five living members (love, faith, perfection, patience, wisdom)
Correspondential objects: Light Mind “comes and finds”; loosening and releasing; binding sin’s mind/thought/insight/counsel/consideration into bone/sinew/vein/flesh/skin; freeing the soul’s members; “new man”; child of righteousness; five great living members; love in mind; faith in thought; perfection in insight; patience in counsel; wisdom in consideration; purifying the image/word; adding his word as nourisher/strengthener.
Spiritual realities: This is regeneration described as a lawful transposition in ultimates.
- To “release the mind of the soul from the bone” is to free the understanding from dead, merely literal or sensuous fixes.
- To “bind sin’s thought in the sinew,” etc., is not annihilation but confinement: evils are relegated to outermost restraints where they cannot rule.
The “new man” is the re-formed natural as an image of heaven: the external now corresponds to the internal. The “five living members” are the restored governing principles:
- Love (celestial) ruling the mind as its heat and end.
- Faith (spiritual) forming the thought as the light of understanding.
- Perfection (spiritual fullness) ordering insight—seeing wholes truly.
- Patience (steadfast good under delay) governing counsel—how the will persists in order.
- Wisdom (truth united to good in life) governing consideration—the prudence of application in ultimates.
The “word” purified is doctrine and speech made clean from falsity; it becomes “nourisher” because true doctrine feeds the natural and strengthens it to resist relapse.
Movement: The chapter reaches its center: salvation is the rearrangement of rule. The Light Mind does not merely forgive; it reassigns seats of power in the ultimate faculties, freeing what is human and binding what is hellish, then building a new correspondent form.

¶41–43 — Perfection of the twelve; ascent to heights; old man imprisoned; occasional clouding and doubt
Correspondential objects: twelve members perfected; running a road/path; mounting to heights and aeons; old man bound; dark spirit imprisoned; reign by love/faith/perfection/patience/wisdom; Light Mind king over totality; affliction arises; sin mounts up; disturbs consideration; clouds wisdom/understanding; truth split into doubt; foolish words.
Spiritual realities: “Twelve” signifies all things of faith and charity in completeness and order; perfection of the twelve is the full organization of the regenerated life in ultimates. “Road/path” is the doctrine of life—how truth is walked. “Mounting to heights” is elevation into higher degrees (spiritual, and toward celestial) when the natural corresponds.
Yet “affliction” and periodic clouding show the continuing presence of the proprium at the boundaries: temptations and obscurities allowed so the new order is confirmed. “Truth split into doubt” is the natural’s oscillation when lower remnants stir; it does not disprove kingship, but marks combat at the extremes.
Movement: Regeneration culminates in ascent and ordered reign, but remains a guarded kingdom: disturbances recur at the perimeter, requiring continued governance.

¶51–55, 57 — The conclusion: invisibility of watch-keepers and Mind; accommodation (becoming small); purity without defilement; active government; appearance only to the opened eye
Correspondential objects: opened eyes; confusion in the zone as analogy; watch-keepers not visible; Mind not visible; great ones “contorted/bent… become small” to the measure of the task; transcendent and purified yet in mingling not defiled; Mind vast over watch-districts; stays fast at his camp; shuts off deliberations from beguilements; limits/distributes; “open and perceptive eye” for appearance.
Spiritual realities: Spiritual governors are not objects of natural sight because they are interior causes, seen only by enlightenment. “Becoming small” is accommodation: higher truth bending itself into natural forms without losing its purity (like light entering a dark room—remaining light, though received according to the room). “Mingling” without defilement is the law of influx: what is pure remains pure in itself, though the recipient may distort; hence the need for “limiting and distributing”—the Mind’s providential management of thoughts and affections so sin cannot beguile.
Appearance depends on the organ: the “opened eye” is an enlightened understanding; without it, the Light Mind’s operations are unseen though real.
Movement: The chapter seals its argument: the Light Mind is present as ruling influx, not as a visible figure. Its greatness is shown precisely in governance within ultimates—restraining, distributing, ordering—while remaining untainted. Perception of this is itself a gift of enlightenment.

ONE CONTINUOUS SPIRITUAL NARRATIVE
The chapter describes the descent of Divine truth (Light Mind) into the natural man and the lawful manner in which the Infinite acts in the finite. The natural mind is a “body of flesh” already inhabited by the hereditary proprium (“old man”) and by sin’s installed governance in the outer faculties. Therefore the presence of Light does not immediately abolish disturbance; rebellions recur as the outermost plane is fought over.
To answer why such disorders occur, the text first unveils a universal law: even the total system of the worlds is arranged in the form of a Man, because all created order is human in form; yet in opposite sense the enemy constructs a counterfeit Grand Man—an apparent harmony whose ruling love is inverted. Watch-keepers are then stationed through discrete degrees—above and below—to stabilize influx: counsel governs wind (influx), fire (love), and water (truth in the natural), while the Porter guards the threshold in ultimates. Still, when lower things are permitted to act “for a moment,” treacheries erupt: falsity tangles with the soul’s light, agitation rises in the sea of knowledges, lust populates the earth of the natural, paths of ascent are blocked, and ultimate fastenings loosen.
Providence answers by deeper descent: binding powers with chains (fixed general truths), bringing forth the Pillar of Glory to bear the burden in ultimates, and sending accommodated Divine truth (Jesus) into the lowest affections and foundations to straighten the tracks of influx, reopen springs of wind/water/fire, and restore the pathways of ascent. Thus the macrocosmic pattern is disclosed as the microcosmic process of regeneration.
Finally the work is shown in its precise correspondential mechanics: sin had bound the soul’s faculties into outer tissues (bone, sinew, vein, flesh, skin) and enthroned its own counterfeit powers upon them. The Light Mind reverses the bondage—freeing the soul’s members and confining sin’s members to the outermost restraints—then constructs a new man in which love, faith, perfection, patience, and wisdom are seated as living governors. When the whole (twelve) is ordered, the person is elevated; the old man is imprisoned, though peripheral afflictions and clouds of doubt may still arise at times.
The chapter ends by teaching that this kingship is not ordinarily visible: like unseen watch-keepers, the Light Mind is known by its operations—limiting, distributing, restraining beguilements—not by outward display. It remains pure while accommodated to the mixed natural. It “appears” only to the opened eye: an understanding enlightened to see causes within effects, and the Divine order within the body’s smallness.

fills.notes: The sentence contrasts the Light Mind as "one among the gods" with the accompaniment of a plurality. The oldest layer typically uses a simple connective here rather than a named hierarchy; "and" preserves the impersonal, structural register.
The third question asks for an account reconciling purity/holiness with bodily defilement. The oldest-layer register frames it as an explanatory "How" rather than devotional petition.

The question’s correspondential burden is: pure influx accommodated to impure ultimates without being defiled. The gap must introduce the mechanism: purity remaining untainted while present in the defiled body.
"Unveiled" pairs naturally with "spoken" in this substrate: revelation is disclosure in discourse, not liturgical proclamation.

The line contrasts what has already been unveiled "in our presence" with the request to know the Light Mind "the way that he is"—i.e., in essence. A coordination with "and" fits the didactic, non-devotional tone.
The speaker resumes with a conditional repetition/recapitulation; "again" is the expected connective in this teaching style.
Fits the didactic thrust: the promised "vision" depends on the hearer’s capacity to understand correspondentially, not on outward display.
The stomach as "five unfolded ones" requires an apposition clarifying them as folds/compartments of the garments—cosmic layers arranged as coverings.
From navel to hip = the connecting stretches from the central sphere to the quarters. "Extensions" matches the correspondence: derivations from the central knowledges to the four-world corners.
Loins correspond to generative ultimates; the three earths are "set" beneath the Porter. The substrate uses simple placement verbs for cosmological stationing.
Parallel to "set": the three earths are not transient but fixed as supports under the Porter (gate-function).
Between loins and shins, thighs correspond to the broad supports connecting higher ultimates to lower. The text then immediately continues "from the ... to the earth"—a span term like "breadth" fits.
Shins/feet are lowest supports; "mountains" as raised ultimates (in opposite sense, rigid elevations in the natural) commonly appear as part of the earth’s structure.
Completes the clause "and the entire zone that belongs ..."—the zone is distributed to the four directions/worlds, matching the earlier "corners of the four worlds."
Outer skin as enclosing wall: the correspondence demands an enclosing/stretching boundary around the dangerous fire-perimeter.
The anatomy-to-cosmos mapping typically pairs outer/inner skins: outer wall; inner as vessels/containers. This keeps the ordered body-correspondence.
Between skins and gall/intestines, a divider/partition is expected: midriff/diaphragm corresponds to separating boundary within the fiery region.
A receptacle correspondence is demanded before the intestines/breadth. "Storehouse" suits the cosmological containment register.
Ears correspond to reception; in cosmos-body mapping, winds/breath are the natural correspondents of influx/utterance. Fits the later wind-track/springs theme.
Feet already mentioned; a final detail like toes fits the body-schema completion in this catalogue.
The worlds are "harmonised" by being fixed in stations; "made to stand" matches the watch-keeper/foundation theme.
Harmony in this system is fastening/binding—key vocabulary throughout (chains, fastenings, binding).
Introduces the causal explanation that follows: five gods fastened in him, etc.
The line moves toward the salvific mechanism (Living Spirit/Ambassador/guardians). The substrate often marks the provisional state "until" release occurs.
Each watch-keeper clause begins "He has ..."; the first missing phrase should be the generic stationing verb.
Keeper of Splendour is a fixed governor "set firm" above the prison; "set fast" maintains the restraint/fastening vocabulary.
The mind "above" is enclosed/terminated in its firmament-station; enclosure is the chapter’s solution to "great in the small."
Introduces "whole ... of the powers"; required for grammatical completion.
Powers of heaven are "in" a camp/watch-district; keeps the military-station metaphor stripped of later ecclesial tone.

Adamant of Light is explicitly "insight"; the gap should complete that apposition cleanly in oldest-layer terminology.
In the standard layered schema, thought in the seventh; insight in the sixth; counsel in the fifth; etc. This preserves discrete-degree architecture.
King of Glory is "counsel" paired with patience; the lacuna sits inside "counsel ... patience" and should provide the connective continuation.
He exercises authority over the three images/wheels; "set over" matches the pattern of appointments.
Echoes immediately "that of wind, that of fire, and that of water"; restoring the referent maintains coherence.
He is given something "to do evilness"—i.e., to curb it, not commit it. Oldest substrate frames governance as restraint/limitation.
Marks transition to the Porter appointment, maintaining the catalogue rhythm.
Parallelism: each governor is "appointed"; redundancy is typical of this register.
The Porter is wisdom/consideration "below"; the foundation is beneath all. This completes the downward discrete-degree placement.
Camps are made strong "so that" each is secure; in the substrate the securing cause is ordinance/order rather than moral exhortation.
Sin mixed with light then "went" to the third firmament; a rising motion fits the correspondential surge before descent to dry/moist.
"watch-tower" must govern/locate the Keeper of Splendour; completing as "watch-tower of the Keeper" maintains spatial hierarchy.
Thought "made ... with wrath" demands a verb of ignition; wrath corresponds to perverted fire.
After "destruction, on the earth" the clause "... to it" needs an augmenting phrase: ruin added to the earth from the watchers’ acts.
Begins the section: "The Adamant ... the fulfillment"; requires the genitive completion to specify the entity.

Completes "set firm upon ..." in the descending degree-series: Adamant/insight placed in the sixth (above) earlier; here a watch associated with Adamant may be set upon the fifth/its station. Some uncertainty remains due to compression.
The three earths are "pained and oppressed"—an intensifier is expected before the doublet.
"paths closed" to their ... : in this schema, ways/roads of ascent are closed to the powers in the three earths.
Connects impediments: ascent impeded ... and wind/water/fire ascend. Simple connective fits.
"Porter, he who humiliates ..." requires an object: humiliates the great uprising of the abysses—i.e., brings it low.
Connects uprising with resulting bending/loosening of fastenings.
"fastenings underneath were loosened" needs auxiliary; restores straightforwardly.
"came forth; as it ... helper" requires a passive/causative: Pillar of Glory was made/helper appointed.
The descent is by the accommodated saving figure already identified as "Jesus the Youth" in ¶17; oldest layer uses functional epithet rather than NT overlay.
"he sent Jesus ... the prayer" requires an instrumental: through/by means of the prayer of the five sons.
"He assumed them ... the abortions": the saved elements are taken out from among the abortions—separation by selection.
Fastenings that "... because of this": they were beneath the earth/Porter and got loosened; required referent for strengthening beneath.
"came up to his ... rest": the idiom is return to the place/station of rest, i.e., proper degree after descent.
Watch-keepers/gods master "watching over them" in fixed stations; fits the theme of being set fast yet subject to uprisings in their districts.
The repeated disturbances in the macrocosm are earthquakes/treacheries; "earthquakes" anticipates the microcosm comparison.
After permitting error "for a moment" the powers "seize"—i.e., take hold of the enmity afterward; this matches providential permission then restraint.
Completes the phrase "with respect to" in the question formula.
"These gods, in that ... are great" needs a locator: they are in the zone/watch-district system; supports the later analogy to body.
The five angels/authorities placed upon the soul’s members then "... , pronouncing"—a participle like "standing" fits as stationed overseers.
"worshipping the things that ... will not remain" demands a description of transient externals; "made of matter" expresses perishability in this register.
"making obeisance ... idols" needs the preposition.
Completes common triad: wood, stone, metals; keeps non-Christian, anti-idolatry polemic in correspondential terms.
Hostility to father follows forgetfulness; hatred expresses inversion of influx (turning from source).
Pairs with previous clause: hostile to father and to itself—closed system of proprium.
"its own light" in the final phrase demands a verb of quenching; corresponds to loss of spiritual illumination.
The Light Mind finds the soul in the state described in ¶37: error/forgetfulness. This anchors the reversal sequence.
After finding, he acts: raising/awakening corresponds to enlightenment preceding loosening of bonds.
"assuming it in the ..." points back to the body as ultimate receptacle where the work of rebinding occurs.
Introduces the means: by his wisdom he becomes liberator.
He becomes for it what he does: loosener of bonds in the five members—matches the correspondential mechanics.

"so that his ... becomes nourisher"—in this register it is the purified utterance/teaching that feeds and strengthens the new man.
Perfection culminates in ordering "the twelve" (totality of truths/goods). A doublet "perfect and order" matches the constructive cadence.
The sentence enumerates love/faith/perfection/patience/wisdom as governing principles; this clause ties the process to those internals.
Immediately paired with love and wisdom in the following: the triad needs naming.
"as he perf[ects ...]" requires an object: the person/new man. "in completeness" resonates with twelve=all things.
Formerly running in disorder; the old life is described as wandering rather than pilgrimage (avoids later overlay).
Now running in ordered doctrine-of-life; straightness corresponds to rectified tracks earlier.
"road and path and his ..."—the third term naturally is work/deed/use, the ultimate expression of doctrine.
Ascent to aeons implies being fixed in higher degree; "established" matches stationing/fastenings vocabulary.

Old man bound in the five bodily members—the same schema as earlier binding/rebinding.
Completes "body" with comma continuation.
"Yet, his king ... the Light Mind" requires copula: king is the Light Mind.
"While the members ..., thus sin is imprisoned"—the missing phrase should assert the secured/ordered state of the members of the new man.

assessment: Most lacunae here are short, mechanical Coptic restorations (letters/particles) and could be filled with strong confidence. Where the gaps affect cosmological body-mapping (¶11–12) or degree-stations (¶14, ¶21), the correspondential structure tightly constrains the function (enclosure, stationing, restraint, accommodation), but not always the exact noun; those reconstructions remain moderate to tentative. Overall, the restored text preserves the oldest-layer impersonal, architectural voice: ordered stationing, binding/loosening, and accommodated influx rather than later devotional framing.
